The size array is tracked but the union step always attaches to whichever root was passed as the second argument, ignoring size entirely, so the order elements are unioned in determines the final shape rather than balance.

find caches the discovered root back onto the immediate parent only, one link at a time, instead of the whole path, so a single find call shortens the chain by at most one step no matter how long it is.

Path compression runs correctly on every find call, but union never compares the size of the two trees before attaching one root to the other, so merging elements in increasing order still builds a chain one node at a time.

Root Cause: Without path compression or union by size, merging a chain in order builds a degenerate tree one node deep per union. find then walks the whole chain, and the structure whose entire selling point is near-constant-time operations becomes linear.

What is the verified root cause?

options.text: The whole point of a segment tree is that internal nodes cache the sums of their subtrees. Writing a leaf without repairing that cache leaves every ancestor holding a sum computed from the old value.

The update function recomputes every ancestor's sum correctly, but it walks up starting from the wrong index, so it repairs the cache for a sibling subtree instead of the one that was actually changed.

Queries recompute the requested range's sum from the leaves directly every time instead of reading cached internal nodes at all, so updates are always reflected but every query pays the full O(n) cost instead of O(log n).
The tree array is sized for exactly n leaves with no extra room for internal nodes, so writing an ancestor's recomputed sum overflows into a neighbouring leaf's slot and corrupts an unrelated value.

options.text: Cyclic references preventing garbage collection in bidirectional pointers.
Every insert into the trie allocates a brand new fixed-size array of child slots even when most of them stay unused, so memory grows with the alphabet size rather than with the data actually stored.
The segment tree is rebuilt from scratch on every update instead of updating in place, so the old tree array is never freed until the next garbage collection cycle happens to run.
Union-find's path compression keeps a separate history of every root a node has ever pointed to for debugging purposes, and that history list is never cleared.
